decision: The language-neutral data-architecture rules (Core Principles 1-7, the anti-pattern list, the Instructions checklist, the analyse-refactor-verify Workflow with its state file, the define-the-types preference order and the generic rationalizations) live once in coding-data-architecture, which routes Python to coding-python-data-architecture and Rust to coding-rust-data-architecture; the language skills hold only mechanisms.

evidence.text: Heading diff of the pre-rename Python skill against the two new files: every heading is present in one of them except the renamed H1; a line-level check of the pre-edit text listed 85 non-verbatim lines, each reviewed as reworded or moved into a Python section. Probes in checklist-20261109-generic-skill.md.

reopen_if: A language skill needs a different workflow or principle numbering than the generic skill holds, or readers of a language skill repeatedly act without loading the generic one.
why: The Python skill was the only home of rules that hold in any language, so a reader working in another language had no skill to load; copying them into each language skill would let the copies drift.

anchors: One case is a boundary, not a shim: a wire format the system MUST still read
decision: Core Principle 7 keeps its ban on compatibility shims and names one boundary case: a wire format the system must still read gets its own versioned wire record, converted once into the domain type, and old-format aliases and defaults live on that record only. A format nothing reads any more is deleted. The rule is stated once here; the Rust skill points at it.

evidence.text: checklist-20261109-review-fixes.md: RED (opus, pre-edit text) reported four contradictions on a persisted v1/v2 scenario and answered the retirement question NONE; GREEN (opus, edited text) quoted Principle 7's boundary case and the Rust pointer, found no contradiction, and answered 'deleted' from the text.

reopen_if: A reviewer meets an old-format reader that is not at a boundary (an alias kept inside domain code) and the boundary case is cited to justify it.
why: The Rust skill prescribed versioned DTOs carrying serde alias and default while Principle 7 forbade aliases and layers accepting old formats, and the Rust skill also said default must never make an old payload parse; a reader had two contradicting rules and no precedence.

anchors: The pin test reads the table object the code reads
decision: The key-set pin for an enum-keyed lookup table reads the table object the code reads, never a copy in the test module or a list of literals.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: two pin tests in a data-architecture run passed by construction (own copy; three literals).

reopen_if: A pin form appears that reads a copy yet still fails when the real table drops a member.
why: A pin comparing the test's own copy with the enum passes whatever the real table holds, so it pins nothing.

anchors: A boundary DECODE table may remain
decision: A read-only table decoding an externally defined wire code into a display word, whose reader refuses unknown codes and takes no decision on the code, is permitted and needs no enum; it is in the analyser NOT-violations list.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: analysers flagged about 20 wire-code decode tables in one pass.

reopen_if: A decode table is found whose code drives a branch, or a reader that does not refuse unknown codes is treated as covered.
why: Analysers flagged such int-keyed decode tables as closed tables needing IntEnums; the skill covered only enum-keyed tables and string spellings, so these had no stated verdict.

anchors: The `<reason>` may be the library's own message for that one error
decision: A refusal's <reason> may be the validation library's own message for that one error; the anti-pattern bans the whole error text and input slices. Stated in the anti-pattern and the analyser NOT-violations list.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: 3 of 8 analysers flagged compliant refusal formatters.

reopen_if: A library's per-error message is shown to carry internal tags, docs URLs or the input.
why: The language-neutral wording read as forbidding the per-error message, and 3 of 8 analysers flagged refusals already in the prescribed form.

anchors: A finding that contradicts a recorded ruling goes to the user, not to a fixer
decision: Before a finding goes into a fix brief, the coordinator checks it against the repo's recorded decisions; a finding contradicting a ruling goes to the user, not a fixer.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: a brief overrode a recorded ruling in a data-architecture run.

reopen_if: Fixers are given the decisions log as part of every brief and shown to check it.
why: A fix brief overrode a recorded repo ruling until a fixer happened to read the log and stopped.

anchors: though a PARAMETER every caller passes a literal to stays a call-site-sweep finding
decision: A string literal inside a user-facing message is excluded, but a parameter every caller passes a literal to stays a call-site-sweep finding even when its value only ends up in a message.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: analysers disagreed on refused(verb)-shaped helpers.

reopen_if: A case where converting such a parameter to an enum is impossible or harmful.
why: Analysers split on whether the message-literal exclusion covered a literal-only parameter; the skill's own refused(verb) example says it does not.

anchors: change every consumer to read the fields by name
decision: A fixer turning a bare tuple into a record changes every consumer to read the fields by name and names each field for what it holds.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: pass 2 of a 100-module run found 7 records still unpacked positionally.

reopen_if: A record type is found where positional unpacking is the intended interface.
why: New records were still unpacked positionally by every consumer, and one field reused a neighbouring field's name for a different thing.

anchors: Print every case's result in both arms before counting any as
decision: The error-surface diff carries one liveness control per entry point (library and CLI separately) and prints every case's result in both arms before counting any as same.

evidence.text: Queued contribution: 20 CLI cases read as same while all raised the same RuntimeError.

reopen_if: A harness design that proves every entry point live from a single control.
why: Library liveness inputs passed while 20 CLI cases raised one identical error in every arm and read as same.

anchors: keeps what the walk did with every
turns a defaulted field into a dropped row and an unread form into a lost
decision: A DoD item requires a boundary model that replaced a .get() walk to keep what the walk did with every malformed shape (kept, skipped, defaulted), tabulated before the first edit and pinned in tests that pass on the old code first, unless the change is deliberate and listed in the CHANGELOG.

evidence.text: Queued lesson: a data-architecture refactor needed two review rounds to find three behaviour changes (a null archived field dropped the whole row, one non-string label dropped the record, an HTTP-date Retry-After no longer counted as a rate limit) while every existing test stayed green. Re-checked here only by reading: STEP C item 5 diffs exception type, exit code and last error line, which a silent drop does not change.

reopen_if: The error-surface diff in STEP C is extended to compare the parsed output (rows kept, values defaulted) as well as refusals, making a separate DoD item redundant.
why: The DoD covered only the opposite direction (a faithful port keeping an old bug). A strict model inside a skip-on-failure loop turns a defaulted field into a dropped row and an unread value form into a lost signal without raising anything, so the suite and the error-surface diff, which compares exception type, exit code and error line, both read it as unchanged.

anchors: runs on every path where a stored copy of that value re-enters
Each read-back is a boundary too
decision: A DoD item requires a check the live input path applies to a value to run on every path where a stored copy re-enters (cache hit, HTTP 304 from an ETag cache, state read back from disk), by putting the check in the boundary model's validation and parsing every read-back through that model, with a test of a poisoned cache hit.

evidence.text: Queued lesson: the cached next-page URL of an HTTP 304 reply skipped the host check the live 200 path applied, a security finding caught only by a second review round.

reopen_if: coding-input-sanitization gains the same rule and this item is reduced to a pointer there.
why: A check run beside the parse on the live path only is skipped on a cache hit, so a value validated once and stored comes back unchecked. coding-input-sanitization does not state that a stored copy re-entering is a boundary either.

anchors: Keep `--contents`: from pass 2 on STEP B's fixes are uncommitted until STEP C
grep the repo for an older copy of the same rule and count the pair in scope
decision: SCOPE attributes findings with git blame --contents <file> <base>..HEAD -- <file>, and counts a new duplicate of an older rule in scope together with its old twin.

evidence.text: Scratch repo: with an uncommitted line inserted at the top, plain base..HEAD blame gave HEAD's line 1, --contents gave the working-tree line (00000000) and kept ^ on the base lines.

reopen_if: STEP B commits each fix before the next STEP A.
why: From pass 2 on, STEP B's fixes are uncommitted, so a plain base..HEAD blame numbers HEAD's file and misattributes; blame alone files a new duplicate of a pre-base rule as out of scope.
